title: Graphical Representations of Summary Statistics for One Quantitative Variable
rights: Original instructor-authored material; no College Board copyrighted questions or answer keys.

items.prompt: Seven ordered practice scores are 4, 6, 8, 8, 9, 12, 14. Under the median-of-halves convention excluding the overall median, which is the five-number summary?
items.hint: The overall median is the fourth value. Remove it, then take medians of the lower three and upper three.
items.solution: A. Minimum 4, Q1=median(4,6,8)=6, overall median 8, Q3=median(9,12,14)=12, maximum 14. These are scores and should be labelled as such.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14

items.prompt: The nine ordered travel distances, in kilometres, are 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 20. Find the IQR using the median-of-halves convention that excludes the overall median.
items.hint: Exclude the central 8. Average 4 and 5 for Q1, then 12 and 14 for Q3.
items.solution: The lower half 2,4,5,6 has median Q1=(4+5)/2=4.5 km. The upper half 10,12,14,20 has median Q3=(12+14)/2=13 km. IQR=13−4.5=8.5 km.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14

items.prompt: For the nine workshop journeys 5, 8, 10, 12, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18 minutes, calculate the UPPER 1.5-IQR fence in minutes using the chapter's quartile convention.
items.hint: Q1=9, Q3=15.5; upper fence is Q3+1.5×IQR.
items.solution: IQR=15.5−9=6.5 minutes. Upper fence U=15.5+1.5(6.5)=25.25 minutes. This is a screening boundary, not necessarily an observed time.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14

items.prompt: The sorted times 5, 8, 10, 12, 12, 14, 15, 16, 50 minutes have upper 1.5-IQR fence 25.25. Where should the RIGHT whisker end in a MODIFIED boxplot? Enter the observed value in minutes.
items.hint: Do not draw the whisker to the fence or to the flagged 50. Which time is the largest non-outlier?
items.solution: The 50-minute time lies beyond the upper fence, so plot 50 separately. The largest observed non-outlier is 16 minutes; the right modified whisker ends at 16.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14

items.prompt: Which feature is most likely to be visible in a dotplot or histogram but hidden in a boxplot?

options.label: D
options.text: The approximate location of the quartiles

items.hint: A boxplot retains a few summary landmarks, not every individual point.
items.solution: C. A boxplot preserves the five landmarks (and potentially outlier markings) but cannot reliably communicate the number of peaks or gaps. Use a dotplot/histogram to study detailed shape.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14

items.prompt: Which statement is generally accurate for a strongly right-skewed quantitative distribution?

options.label: A
options.text: The mean is usually larger than the median, but this is not a universal test.

options.label: B
options.text: The mean is always smaller than the median.

options.label: C
options.text: The mean and median must be exactly equal.

options.label: D
options.text: If the mean exceeds the median, the distribution must be right-skewed.

items.hint: Think about how exceptionally high observations affect the sum and the ranked middle value.
items.solution: A. A long right tail often pulls the mean above the median. It is only a tendency: mean greater than median is not a sufficient condition for right skew.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14

items.prompt: Two hypothetical groups' travel times are in minutes. Group A has five-number summary (2, 4, 6, 8, 10); Group B has (2, 3, 6, 9, 10). Compare medians and middle-half variability using numbers, and explain one conclusion that is NOT justified by these summaries.
items.hint: Compare both medians, then subtract Q1 from Q3. Ask whether a cause or entire shape can be inferred.
items.solution: Both groups have median 6 minutes. Group A has IQR=8−4=4 minutes, whereas Group B has IQR=9−3=6 minutes, so Group B's central half is more variable by 2 minutes. The summaries alone cannot identify causes of the difference, reveal gaps/modes, or establish a population-level difference.
items.rubric: Award credit for the equal median (6 minutes), both correctly computed IQRs (4 and 6 minutes), an in-context comparison, and an explicit valid limitation.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14

items.prompt: Construct a modified boxplot on a number line for 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 30 minutes. State the five-number summary, IQR, numerical fences, actual whisker endpoints, and any separate outlier marker. Explain the difference between fence and whisker.
items.hint: The median is 7; halves are 3,4,5,6 and 8,9,10,30. Check whether 30 crosses the upper fence.
items.solution: Minimum 3, Q1=(4+5)/2=4.5, median 7, Q3=(9+10)/2=9.5, maximum 30 minutes. IQR=5. Fences are L=4.5−7.5=−3 and U=9.5+7.5=17 minutes. Draw a box from 4.5 to 9.5 with median at 7; left whisker to observed 3, right whisker to observed 10; mark 30 separately as a potential outlier. The fence 17 is a boundary, not an observation.
items.rubric: Include all five numbers; calculate IQR/fences accurately; label axis in minutes; show whiskers at 3 and 10, not −3 and 17; plot outlier 30 separately; explain the distinction.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14

items.prompt: Hypothetical travel times in minutes are 1, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39. What is the sample mean in minutes? Enter your answer to two decimals.
items.hint: Sum all nine observations and divide by nine. Compare the result with median 35.
items.solution: Sum=285 minutes, n=9; mean=285/9≈31.67 minutes, less than median 35. The low observation contributes to a long left tail; the mean–median pattern is a tendency, not a proof of skewness.
items.provenance: Original Maple Hill School hypothetical question, 2026-10-14
